question.text: If \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) are two complex numbers satisfying the equation \(\left|\frac{z_1+z_2}{z_1-z_2}\right|=1\), then \(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\) may be

solution.text:
Hint : \(\left|\frac{z_1+z_2}{z_1-z_2}\right|=1\) \(\left|z_1 / z_2+1\right|=\left|z_1 / z_2-1\right|\)
Distance of \(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\) from -1 and 1 are equal So, locus of \(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\) is perpendicular bisector of line joining \((-1,0) ~\&~(1,0)\) \(\therefore \frac{\boldsymbol{z}_1}{\mathbf{z}_2} \Rightarrow\) purely imaginary or 0
